solution: Scan the scoreboard from rank 1 downward keeping a hash set of universities already represented; a team is a winner exactly when its university is new, and the first twelve such teams get the four first, four second and four third prizes. Because only the best-placed team of each university may be awarded and ranks arrive in order, the greedy scan is forced: skipping a new university could only be replaced by a lower-ranked team of the same university, which is never allowed. At least twelve distinct universities are guaranteed, so twelve teams always exist. O(N) time and O(N) space for N<=200 lines.
statement_summary: A contest scoreboard lists up to two hundred teams in finishing order, each line giving the team's university and its name. Only the highest-placed team of any university may win a prize, and exactly twelve prizes are handed out. The task is to print the twelve prize-winning teams, in scoreboard order, given that at least twelve distinct universities appear.
notes: Trivial filtering scan; the prize tiers (4/4/4) are flavour and never affect the output. No greedy label: nothing is being optimised, the selection is forced. verify_icpcawards.py checks the statement's 30-team sample and an independent O(N^2) reimplementation on random boards.
